subject: SIG questionnaire: telemetry proof, sampled logs, and closure plan
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acmetech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: audit@acmetech.com
Date: 2027-09-12T14:02:00Z
Subject: SIG controls — telemetry samples and proof request

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for taking our SIG follow-up. As part of the control substantiation we need: 

- Sample telemetry extracts covering authentication events, key management access, and inference request audit (time window: one week).
- Mapping that shows which Redwood control IDs correspond to SIG/CSA items (a simple two-column CSV is fine).
- Any attestation language you provide about retention windows and redaction processes.

Can you confirm what artifacts you can provide, how they will be sanitized, and whether you can deliver a sample bundle by 2027-09-20? I attached a CSV with the scope we typically ask for.

Best,
Sara
Sara Liu
Lead IT Auditor — AcmeTech

Attachment: acmetech_requested_sample_scope.csv (CSV, 2KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acmetech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-13T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG controls — telemetry samples and proof request

Hi Sara,

Appreciate the clear scope — that's helpful. Short answer: we can provide a curated, redacted telemetry bundle plus a control-mapping CSV and a short attestation for the items you listed. Proposed approach: 

1) Produce a filtered export for the requested week containing:
   - Auth logs (success/failure) with user-ids hashed,
   - Key management access summary (KMS operation records, no plaintext keys),
   - Inference audit: request_id, model_id, timestamp, request size (tokens), and synthetically masked prompt snippets.

2) Deliverables:
   - control_mapping_ACME.csv (Redwood control ID -> SIG entry),
   - telemetry-bundle-REDUCED.tar.gz (manifest + sample files),
   - redaction-attestation.txt signed by InfoSec.

3) Sanitation: we'll hash internal user IDs, truncate prompt text to 64 chars, remove IP addresses, and remove any customer-specific identifiers. Legal will review the redaction approach.

We plan to stage the artifacts to a secure shared folder and provide a downloadable DocuSign NDA when needed. Tentative timeline: internal bundle ready by 2027-09-18, final sanitized bundle by 2027-09-20 pending legal signoff.

Karthik / Mina / Jonas — can you confirm the retention windows and the easiest export path? If there are any blockers please call them out.

Thanks,
Irene
Director, Security Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@acmetech.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-13T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG controls — telemetry samples and proof request

Irene / Sara — quick technical notes: 

- Retention: auth logs and inference audit events are stored for 90 days in our telemetry cluster; KMS operation metadata is stored for 365 days as part of our KeyOps ledger.
- Export path: we can run a filtered export job that produces NDJSON and a manifest. The export will be scoped by tenant tag; since AcmeTech is a hosted customer we'll generate a tenant-scoped bundle (no cross-tenant data).
- Sanitization: we recommend the following pipeline: PII redaction -> tokenization (hash email/username) -> sample truncation -> manual review of the manifest. This pipeline is automated but requires a brief manual QA pass (~2 hours).

I'll kick off the export once legal confirms the redaction profile. Attaching a short manifest template and the small manifest file we'll use.

Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@acmetech.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T08:37:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG controls — telemetry samples and proof request

Sara / team — security acceptance criteria and items from our side: 

- Artifacts we will include:
  * auth_events.ndjson (hashed_user, event_type, ts, result)
  * kms_operations.csv (operation, principal_hash, ts, key_id_redacted)
  * inference_audit_sample.jsonl (request_id, model_id, ts, token_count, prompt_masked)
  * telemetry-bundle-manifest.txt (file list + SHA256 digests)

- Acceptance criteria:
  * No plaintext credentials, keys, or customer PII in delivered files.
  * Manifest present with checksums and description of redaction rules.
  * Signed attestation (redaction-attestation.txt) confirming the above.

I've attached our redaction-guidance-template.pdf for your review. Legal prefers that AcmeTech sign our limited-scope NDA/POA for artifact access — we'll put the DocuSign link in the delivery folder.

If Acme needs more raw detail we'll propose a monitored review session instead of pushing raw exports.

Mina
Head of InfoSec
